output.headline: US and China extend trade truce as Trump greets Xi Jinping on the tarmac to open state visit
output.standfirst:
Treasury secretary announces extension of ‘Busan agreement’ pausing trade war hostilities as president takes the rare step of laying out the red carpet for Chinese leader at Joint Base Andrews

  • AI, trade, Taiwan and climate: what will and won’t be on agenda at Trump-Xi summit
output.bodyHtml:
Donald Trump has welcomed Xi Jinping to the US at the start of the Chinese leader’s state visit to Washington, taking the unusual step of greeting him in person on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews on the day the two countries agreed to extend their trade truce.

A lavish arrival ceremony met Xi’s plane, with a 30-metre-long (100ft) red carpet flanked by US service members, a military flyover by two B-1 bombers and a presentation of the flags and national anthems of both countries.

Trump and the first lady, Melania, travelled to the military base in Maryland, just outside Washington, to personally shake hands with Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday evening – a departure from the usual practice of US presidents welcoming foreign leaders at the White House.

Related: AI looms large over Trump-Xi meeting amid deep distrust between US and China

Xi’s visit coincides with world leaders gathering in New York for the United Nations general assembly, although the Chinese leader will not address the meeting. He has attended the UNGA just once since becoming president in 2012.

Richard Gowan of the International Crisis Group told Reuters: “It’s pretty notable that Xi Jinping is ⁠coming to Washington in the same week as the general assembly, but does not feel bothered to come up to New York,” he said. “I think a lot of people will say: ‘Where is the real center of decision-making?’”

The US and China agreed on Wednesday to extend the so-called Busan agreement – a temporary trade truce between the world’s two biggest economies – Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, announced.

The agreement will now run until 10 January, two months beyond the date it was due to expire, Bessent told Fox News after meeting the Chinese vice-premier He Lifeng earlier on Wednesday.

The pageantry continues with a formal state welcome on the South Lawn of the White House, private tea with the US president and first lady, and a tour of the National Archives, among other special events.

Over the two-day visit Trump and Xi will take up the simmering trade war alongside many other thorny issues, including the race in artificial intelligence development and geopolitical instability.

The White House has invited major tech leaders, such as executives from OpenAI, Apple, xAI, Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta and others, to a state dinner being held for Xi on Thursday.

The carefully orchestrated arrival ceremony had one discordant note: Trump visibly winced at the sound of a US military jet flying overhead as he stood alongside Xi on the red carpet, listening to the US national anthem. Video of the moment showed that while Trump recoiled from the sound of the flyover, Xi remained impassive, as did the wives of both men.

The moment was captured on a White House livestream and widely mocked online, though it was not included in the edited highlights of the ceremony released by Trump’s aides later.

The US and China have long competed to develop increasingly powerful technology, and the race to further AI has become a major topic among tech companies – especially since several executives came forward to warn about the dangers of rapid development.

Trump has dismissed concerns that AI development could harm people, promoting instead more investment in the technology so the US can beat China in the race.

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so,” Trump wrote on Truth Social last week.

Leading AI development also means leading the world militarily and economically, the president and members of the administration have insisted – further raising the stakes for the US and China.

Xi’s visit is expected to be filled with ceremonial displays, reciprocating the treatment Trump received when he visited China earlier this year.

Trump’s decision to greet the Chinese leader at his plane, rather than at the White House, shows how far the US president is willing to go to honour Xi.

“He’s coming on our soil,” Melania Trump said of the visit to Fox & Friends on Wednesday morning, “and we need to welcome them with the most respect.”

Robert Mackey contributed reporting
